title: Hendrik Witbooi
summary: Hendrik Witbooi was a Nama captain who resisted German colonial rule in South West Africa. UNESCO says that between 1884 and 1894 he tried to forge a united front against German protection treaties. After serving alongside the Germans during the Herero rising, he declared war on them on 3 October 1904 and died of wounds in October 1905. Sources differ on his birth year and death place.

uncertainty.note: UNESCO gives born ca.1835, SAHO 1830 and EBSCO c. 1825. SAHO gives death on 29 October 1905 and notes another source says 28 October.

as_recorded.value: Hendrik Witbooi was born into a prominent Nama family in 1830.
On 29* October 1905, Hendrik Witbooi died in a skirmish with the Germans near Keetmanshoop.
Hendrik Witbooi (c. 1825-1905), chief of the Nama people, r. 1888-1905

where.modern_name: Gibeon, Hardap Region, Namibia (proxy pin: the Witbooi Nama base where the 1904 war began)
where.historical_name: Gibeon, Witbooi Nama territory in German South West Africa

importance.justification: UNESCO calls him a key figure in Namibian history and inscribed his letter journals in the Memory of the World Register.

audience_note: Context includes the German war against the Herero and Nama, widely described as genocide.

reviewer_note: Birth year conflicts across three pages (1825, 1830, 1835), so the start carries +/-5 years. Death place conflicts: SAHO event page says near Keetmanshoop, SAHO timeline says an attack near Vaalgras on 29 October; the pin is therefore Gibeon, where the SAHO timeline places the 4 October 1904 attack on the church, not the death place. Whether Gibeon was his residence is not stated on a page I opened.
